rationale: Codex self-review of the CLI Usage and Where the Money Goes migration to LiteLLM spend. Reviewed the new port across every adapter, coverage clipping, caller access propagation, NULL-safe projection/context reconciliation in one database snapshot, cache versioning, nested typed cache deserialization, and classification/allocation using ledger money. The local projection-only case and subsequent partial raw restore were checked against real PostgreSQL data; attribution sums matched the CLI spend-group total exactly. New strict-lint issues were fixed before publication. This is a self-review, not an independent reviewer approval. Babysit follow-up: reproduced all four CI failures, fixed the decoded-cache capacity to retain two complete analyses including CLI evidence, and updated stale cache-version/summary expectations. Added CLI widget regressions for scoped clipped reads, ledger-only amounts, typed cache round-trips, unavailable retry and inactive coverage. The Usage Attribution folder passes: 734 passed in 20.38s (poetry run pytest -q --no-cov tests/codemie/service/usage_attribution). Sonar follow-up: documented the six intentionally unused ledger-protocol parameters using the existing inline S1172 exception convention, and extracted ledger context accumulation from the classification-input builder to reduce nesting without changing its behavior. Targeted widget/summary checks pass: 53 passed in 4.41s (poetry run pytest -q --no-cov tests/codemie/service/usage_attribution/spend_widgets tests/codemie/service/usage_attribution/test_handler.py::TestSummaryFromTheLedger). Remote build/test stage passed on the previous commit; the Sonar rerun remains pending for this follow-up.
risk_flags: make test-harness stopped before collection because CODEMIE_API_DOMAIN is not configured; there is no local test-harness configuration file.
Repository, branch and client context requires a bounded raw ledger aggregation; local verification does not establish production-scale query performance.

Historical hourly spend without raw repository metadata remains unclassified unless existing allocation rules can assign it. Independent cent rounding can leave a one-cent difference across displayed category rows.

business_review.notes: CLI category amounts, allocations and money-flow slices use the ledger. Elasticsearch remains classification evidence. Shared-project candidate discovery and potential chargeback, Repository Groups, Who Pays and other analysis views keep their existing sources. No local dump, restored data, local configuration or restore script is included.

standards_review.notes: CliUsageSpend follows SpendWidget with a frozen typed output, one cached public read, shared scope and coverage handling, and private classification helpers. Data access stays behind SpendService, SpendLedger and SpendLogsRepository.

The new SQL read applies narrowed_by_access using WidgetContext.scope. No API keys, request payloads or raw ledger rows are added to API responses or committed review evidence. A reviewer /sanity run is requested because this adds an access-scoped analytics read.
